text:
Sam W: Heads-up — profiling on Dedicated NVLink boxes shows KV cache memory creeping during very long-context runs (~60k tokens).

Anya P: Is that reclaim lag or fragmentation?

Miguel R: Pattern looks like reclaim lag amplified by fragmentation. Evict tasks are being delayed by networking/kernel waits in some VPC configs.

Sam W: Exactly. Hosted clusters use kv.evict_window_ms=200, but Dedicated pools were left at 800 from an old tuning pass. Private on-prem boxes are at 250 but run an older kernel/driver, so we see page-splitting and higher fragmentation.

Priya S: Do we have a flamegraph or perf sample?

Sam W: Quick perf snippet I grabbed from canary Dedicated node: 
```
# perf summary (sample)
kv_reclaim 42%
page_free 18%
kernel_waits (netlink/futex) 9%
fallback_kernel (generic_matmul) 6%
```
Also saw batching fallback to generic kernels once KV working set hit a threshold, which drives CPU up and delays frees.

Anya P: Two vectors then: reduce eviction window + try early compaction on reclaim. Worth an A/B on Hosted vs Dedicated.

Miguel R: For Private staging repro, driver 510 shows hugepage misalignment causing small leftover slabs -> fragmentation accumulates across long contexts. NVLink remote pinning makes it worse.

Sam W: Proposed experiment: set kv.evict_window_ms=100 on a canary Dedicated pool, enable kv.reclaim_coalesce=true, and adjust batching heuristic to prefer smaller micro-batches (<=32 tokens per GPU) for long-context runs to keep peak KV footprint down.

Priya S: Add metrics too: kv_free_latency_ms histogram and prefix_reuse_ratio in Console so we can correlate memory plateaus with reclaim latency and reuse.

devops-bot: deploy started for canary-dedicated-3 (kv.evict_window_ms=100, kv.reclaim_coalesce=true) :rocket:

deploy-bot: rollout success on canary-dedicated-3 (3/3 hosts), smoke 30m — no OOMs.

Miguel R: Early signals look positive — memory plateaued instead of linear growth on the 60k token workload.

Anya P: Next step: run 100k token end-to-end on Private staging after driver bump + enable reclaim_coalesce, and compare host-level fragmentation metrics (slab_free / allocated_frag_ratio).

Sam W: I'll add the perf harness and a short runbook for engineers to repro locally (nvlink vs pcie toggles). If Private still shows issues we should consider a kernel/driver advisory for customers.

Priya S: Nice. If this stabilizes Dedicated, we should sync the Hosted defaults to the safer values and add an Optimize suggestion (auto-lower evict_window for long-context workloads). :white_check_mark:

Sam W: Thanks — creating a short ticket and will paste logs/graphs there.
